end.summary:
Practised drawing and interpreting square-number dot patterns.
Used pictures to explain how a sequence grows between terms.
Correctly identified 4×4 and 5×5 squares as 16 and 25 dots.
Explained that a shared corner is counted twice and must be subtracted once.
The added-dot count remained inconsistent for later examples; no final correction was recorded.
end.parentNote: Asha practised using dot pictures to show square-number sequences and how one square grows to the next. Ishita used the shared-corner idea and explained that it is counted twice, so one must be subtracted. They mixed up the arithmetic and added-dot totals in later examples, and this was not corrected in the final response. At home, draw a 4×4 square growing to 5×5 and mark the new row and column, counting the shared corner only once.
